author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Veterinarian directory can be narrowed to one specialty
summary: Either form of the veterinarian directory can be asked for one specialty and then lists only the veterinarians holding it, matched on the whole name regardless of letter case. The machine-readable form is reinstated as a supported surface (REQ-VET-003); the narrowing is REQ-VET-004.
acceptance_criteria: REQ-VET-004: given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when either form of the directory is asked for it, then only those veterinarians are listed
REQ-VET-004: given that same specialty named in another letter case, when the directory is asked for it, then the same veterinarians are listed
REQ-VET-004: given only part of a specialty name, when the directory is asked for it, then no veterinarian matches
REQ-VET-004: given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when the directory is asked for it, then the request succeeds and the list is empty
REQ-VET-004: given no specialty, or one that is nothing but spaces, when either form of the directory is opened, then every veterinarian is listed as before
REQ-VET-004: given a narrowed directory spanning more than one page, when a further page is opened, then the narrowing still applies
REQ-VET-003: given the clinic's veterinarians, when the machine-readable directory is requested, then it carries every veterinarian with the specialties each holds
non_goals: a form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing a specialty on either form of the directory
free-text search for a veterinarian, a pet, or a visit (NG-9, narrowed 2026-08-15)
narrowing any other list by an attribute it shows
notes: The owner's stated request-address contract for both surfaces is quoted verbatim in the intake-decision at line 1; read it there rather than from this record. docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for docs/adr/2026-08-15-non-goal-vet-specialty-filter.md — that file is outside this agent's write scope. Two open questions are recorded in the PRD: whether a visible specialty control follows, and whether the machine-readable directory should be paged.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice re-applies the owner-search shape inside the vet feature package: an optional query parameter read by the controller, blank treated as absent, and a Spring Data derived query returning a Page. No new module, layer, or pattern is introduced, so the Package Structure and Contracts sections of docs/system-design.md hold unchanged. Two adjustments distinguish it from the owner precedent. Matching is whole-name and case-insensitive rather than prefix, and the case folding belongs in the query (the IgnoreCase derived-query keyword) rather than in the schema, which is what keeps the three vendor schemas from diverging the way owner search does. Pagination links must carry the parameter, which the owners template does not do. Both surfaces route through the repository so the matching rule exists once. The machine-readable surface is now recorded as serving REQ-VET-003 in the Contracts table, and its Known Defects row is removed.
integration_points: VetRepository gains a specialty-narrowed paged read for /vets.html and a specialty-narrowed unpaged read for /vets; both surfaces call them, so the matching rule lives in one place
vetList.html pagination links gain the specialty parameter; the machine-readable surface stays unpaged per the slice's non-goal
No new user-facing text is needed, since neither surface gains a control; the message-bundle parity test guarding REQ-LANG-002 is unaffected

patterns.description: optional query parameter, stripped, empty treated as the broadest request, then a paged repository call — the shape to mirror for the specialty parameter
derived query returning Page<Owner> with a Pageable — the shape for the specialty-narrowed paged read
@DataJpaTest exercising VetRepository against seeded H2 data — the home for verifying case folding and whole-name matching against a real database
counter-example: owner pagination links carry only page and drop the search term; the vet template must carry specialty on every page link

risks.risk: Annotating the narrowed query with @Cacheable("vets") makes the cache key include a caller-supplied string, and CacheConfiguration creates that cache with no size limit, so arbitrary values grow it without bound
risks.mitigation: Leave the narrowed reads uncached; keep @Cacheable on the two unfiltered reads only

risks.risk: The H2 vet_specialties table declares no unique constraint on (vet_id, specialty_id), unlike the MySQL and PostgreSQL schemas, so a join on specialty name can return a veterinarian more than once
risks.mitigation: Use the Distinct keyword in the derived query so the result is per-veterinarian on every vendor

risks.risk: Case-insensitive matching sought from schema collation would repeat the PostgreSQL divergence recorded under Known Defects for owner search
risks.mitigation: Use the IgnoreCase derived-query keyword, which folds case in JPQL and behaves the same on all three vendors

risks.risk: Adding a fetch join for specialties to the paged query makes Hibernate page the result in memory
risks.mitigation: Keep the implicit join that navigating specialties.name produces; the association is already eager, and the existing paged read has the same shape

risks.risk: VetControllerTests stubs VetRepository, so tests written only there assert case folding and whole-name matching against a stub rather than a database
risks.mitigation: Assert the request-address contract and the empty-list response in VetControllerTests, and the query semantics in ClinicServiceTests

risks.risk: Copying owner search wholesale would carry over its no-result rejection and its single-result redirect, both of which contradict the empty-list-succeeds criterion
risks.mitigation: Render the normal page or document with an empty list and no error

notes: Durable memory updated: docs/adr/README.md gains the index row for the 2026-08-15 non-goal ADR; docs/system-design.md drops the Known Defects row calling the machine-readable route requirement-less, and records REQ-VET-003 against Vets, VetRepository, and VetController. REQ-VET-004 is deliberately not yet in the Implements column — it goes in when the code lands. Residual open question, recorded rather than raised: whether the vets cache should eventually cover narrowed reads. This extends Open Question 5 in docs/system-design.md (no eviction is configured) rather than answering it, and the uncached-narrowed-read guidance above is the narrow reading that needs no product answer. No design-doc-autofix records exist, so the autofix audit found nothing.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Not run, not clean: no OWASP Dependency-Check plugin is configured in build.gradle, and this reviewer has no network access, so no NVD match ran. The resolved framework versions (Spring Boot 4.1.0, Jackson via the BOM) are unverified against the NVD by this review. There is no dependency delta in this change, so nothing here needs to block — but the standing gap is worth closing in CI, and it compounds with the already-recorded open question 6 (no dependency lockfile) in docs/system-design.md.

A very long specialty value is passed through to the query unbounded. It binds as an equality parameter against an indexed column, so there is no injection or ReDoS path, and the neighbouring owner last-name search accepts unbounded free text the same way — pattern-consistent with the baseline. Worth a bound only if request-size limits are ever tightened project-wide.
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the specialty narrowing goes through Spring Data derived query methods (findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase, paged and unpaged) — no query text is concatenated from the request value, so the parameter binds. Swept src/main/java for concatenated/interpolated query text: none in the change.

Cross-site scripting: the request-derived specialty reaches the page only through Thymeleaf link expressions @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialtyFilter})}, which URL-encode the value and escape the attribute. Default output escaping stays on; no th:utext anywhere in templates. Notably the change removes the pre-existing __${...}__ preprocessing from the vetList page links rather than extending it to a request-derived value — the one place preprocessing would have been an expression-injection vector. The surviving __${...}__ usages in owners/, fragments/ are pre-existing and carry only ids and int page counters (baseline, not a finding under docs/security-principles.md § Applying this section).

Boundary validation: asRequestedSpecialty normalizes at the controller boundary (null/empty/whitespace-only all collapse to the whole directory), so the null-vs-value contract the repository and template branch on is established once at the edge rather than re-checked downstream.

Cache abuse: the two narrowed reads are deliberately left off the @Cacheable("vets") cache, with the reason stated inline — the cache has no size limit, so keying it on a caller-supplied string would let an attacker grow it without bound. This is the defensive choice, and the divergence from the neighboring cached findAll carries its justification.

Exposed surface: no new endpoint. Both existing routes (/vets.html, /vets) gain one optional read-only GET parameter that narrows an already-published list; management exposure, auth, and CSRF posture are untouched, so the change is not weaker than the baseline in docs/system-design.md § Security Context.
Unbounded allocation: the JSON route's narrowed read returns a subset of what findAll() already returned unpaged, and the HTML route stays paged at 5 — no new unbounded result set.

Secrets, logging, file I/O, deserialization, process execution: no change. Greps for Runtime/ProcessBuilder/exec(, /tmp/, enableDefaultTyping/@JsonTypeInfo, and credential-shaped identifiers over the diff and src/main/java return nothing introduced here.
Supply chain: build.gradle, gradle/, and pom.xml are unmodified — the change adds no dependency, so the four Adding a New Dependency checks do not apply. Resolution stays on mavenCentral() over TLS.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain was not verified against the NVD in this review: build.gradle configures no OWASP dependency-check plugin (grep for dependencyCheck returns nothing), and this reviewer has no network access. The change adds no dependency and does not touch build.gradle, so the pass carries no new supply-chain exposure, but the standing check on Spring Boot 4.1.0 and its managed Jackson remains un-run here and is left to CI or a human.

Pre-existing, outside this change set: src/main/resources/templates/owners/ownersList.html still builds its pagination links with '__${...}__' preprocessing. The values interpolated there are ints from the model, so there is no exploit path today, but the vets template now demonstrates the safer link-builder form. Converting the owners template on a future pass would leave one way to build a page link across the codebase.
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the specialty reaches persistence only through the Spring Data derived queries VetRepository.findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String) and (String, Pageable). No string-concatenated query text, no JPQL/native query, no LIKE wildcard surface. Matches the mitigation recorded in system-design.md Threat Model for SQL injection.

Template-expression evaluation: the request-derived specialty is never placed in a Thymeleaf preprocessing expression. vetList.html replaced every '__${...}__' page-link with the link-builder form @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialtyFilter})}, which URL-encodes the query-parameter value and HTML-escapes the th:href attribute output. The change removes preprocessing from this template rather than extending it, so no request-derived text can reach expression evaluation.

XSS: specialtyFilter is rendered only inside th:href link expressions (grep for specialtyFilter across src/main/resources and src/main/java returns the 5 template hrefs plus the one model.addAttribute). No th:utext anywhere in src/main/resources/templates; default output escaping stays on.

Cache/DoS: findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase is deliberately left off @Cacheable, with the reason stated in the Javadoc. Verified against CacheConfiguration.java: the 'vets' JCache is created with a bare MutableConfiguration and no size limit, so keying that cache on caller-supplied text would grow unbounded. The uncached choice is the correct fail-secure call, and both overloads make it the same way.

Boundary validation: asRequestedSpecialty normalizes null, empty, and whitespace-only to null at the controller boundary, once, and both endpoints route through it. No unchecked Optional.get, no cast, no null leak into the repository.

Exposed surface unchanged: no new route. /vets.html and /vets each gained one optional @RequestParam of type String. No new binder and no identifier binding, so the mass-assignment control in security-principles.md is untouched. The specialty values were already displayed on the page, so narrowing by one discloses nothing a caller could not already see.

Secrets: grep for password/secret/token/api-key/credential across all five changed Java and template files returns nothing. No logging statement added, so no request text reaches a log line; no new exception message is constructed, so nothing new reaches the error page.
Detection-pattern sweep clean on the changed production surface: no Runtime/ProcessBuilder/exec, no file I/O, no /tmp, no java.util.Random, no Jackson polymorphic-typing config, no XML parsing.
Dependency surface unchanged: build.gradle carries no diff in the change set, so no new dependency and no repository or TLS setting was touched.

author: change-grader
summary: narrow the vet directory by specialty on both surfaces

blast_radius.note: Nine files in one module: the vet feature package (controller, repository interface), its one template, its two test classes, and four docs. No sensitive paths, no build file, no schema, no new route; the 39 hunks are inflated by the five pagination links rewritten one at a time in a template only the vets page uses.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every production hunk and found no behavior beyond the stated contract: asRequestedSpecialty maps null, empty, and whitespace-only to null at one boundary that both endpoints call, the null branch preserves the exact previous findAll calls, and the derived query name findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase gives whole-name case-insensitive matching with no wildcard. The template's th:with narrowed flag omits the parameter entirely when unnarrowed, the new specialtyFilter attribute does not collide with the table loop's specialty variable, and the rewrite of the page links from preprocessing to the link-builder form is a strictly safer construction with identical output.

test_adequacy.note: Tests assert real outcomes rather than restating the code: ClinicServiceTests drives the derived query against seeded H2 and pins the two boundaries a wrong query would break (RaDiOlOgY matches, the prefix radio matches nobody), and VetControllerTests asserts rendered HTML including the page-2 link carrying specialty and its absence when unnarrowed. One residual gap: no test pages a narrowed read across a real page boundary, since the repository test uses Pageable.unpaged() and the pagination test mocks the repository, so the distinct-join count query is only exercised unpaged.

reviewer_hedging.note: Three of four round-2 approvals are clean and findings-free, but the security reviewer's approval parks two recommendations: supply chain was not verified against the NVD (no dependency-check plugin, no network), and owners/ownersList.html still builds page links with the preprocessing form this change removed from the vets template. Neither is in this change set and neither is a reservation about it, but both are residuals the roster deliberately left for a human.

scope_deviation.note: The diff tracks the intake decisions line by line: NG-9 narrowed rather than withdrawn, REQ-VET-003 minted fresh with REQ-VET-002 left withdrawn, no page control added, pagination carrying the parameter, and the two genuinely open choices recorded as open questions instead of decided. The row's design_revisions=1 and build_retries=0 understate the log, which holds three design-block records and one build-failure; reading them, the re-triages were path bookkeeping and a PRD wording fix, not the slice fighting its scope.

rationale: The code read is clean: the boundary normalization, the whole-name case-insensitive query, and the link-builder pagination all do exactly what the requirement says, and the H2-backed tests pin the case and prefix boundaries. The concern is only the security reviewer's two parked recommendations, both outside this change set. Skim the diff, then decide whether to file the owners-template and NVD items as follow-ups.
